argument.native_question: All three exact Tshela keys have the native interior kind for original COG ADM1 Niari, feature ordinal 6, negative ordinal 6. All nine other original operands have empty kinds, including the AGO Cabinda family and COG ADM2 polygons. Those operands remain in the packet; their absence under this predicate is not political clearance.
argument.historical_rule: Actual text of the 23 December 1908 declaration, reproduced in the 1909 bill and approving law of 13 June 1911, identifies the Kiama–Bembo ridge route and recognizes the mixed commission’s whole-frontier map and minutes as its documentary control. Actual Jentgen pages 31–32 and 65–67 distinguish treaty precision from demarcation, and report ratification exchange on 4 April 1912. This is substantive frontier context, but the executed readings do not establish that the three keys lie on that particular ridge subsegment. Manyanga 1903 and the Cabinda 1913 river/pond rules are separate.
argument.source_construction: The exact COG ADM1 source ZIP was obtained, size/hash verified, and its DBF, XML, metadata, and licence image read. Niari is record 6 / CG-9, matching the named original feature. The archive attributes 2017 OSM/Wambacher and documents later field processing, but supplies no OSM relation version or extract snapshot. Name/ISO correspondence is not archive-to-output coordinate equivalence. COD’s atlas digitization and watercourse-splitting history likewise does not establish the disputed modern frontier convention.
argument.mismatch_assessment: The native interior contact now identifies Niari specifically, eliminating the need to use Cabinda or distant COG ADM2 explanations for these holds. Neither the recovered OSM archive nor the declaration demonstrates an erroneous Niari edge or a valid target-side clearance. No historical landmark is georeferenced using unsupported modern coordinates, and no ridge/DEM constructor is introduced.
argument.reasonable_failed_qualification: The earlier ZIP obstacle was resolved by a separately approved exact-source download, so it is not retained as a current blocker. The declaration, approving-law reproduction, Jentgen study, and official AE1 custody descriptions were actually read. The declaration supplies no numeric modern control table. The inspected archive does not identify the OSM history needed to tie a frontier edit to the exact representation. AE1 item 464 / AE(327) and the companion AE(255) descriptions provide custody leads, not an exposed definitive map body; targeted discovery did not identify that digital annex.
argument.proposal_basis: The proposed researched-unresolved treatment rests on a specific failed qualification after actual legal-text, source-archive, and custody investigation. It does not rely on missing metadata alone, pretend that Kiama–Bembo was bound to these cells, or demand an impossible universal sovereignty certificate. These three exact cells can be independently assessed on the completed source-relative work with the remaining historical-control limitation fully visible.
argument.remaining_finite_step: Consult the specifically referenced mixed-commission map/minutes through the AE1 custody route, first verifying that the item covers the relevant Tshela segment and has usable controls. An authenticated OSM relation/extract identity for this consumed Niari feature would be a separate lineage lead if it becomes available. No exact digitized map URL or archive-supplied relation identity was found in the executed work; neither universal absence nor future impossibility is claimed.
argument.scope_exclusions: Cabinda primary readings do not qualify Niari. The 1903 Manyanga marker set does not automatically bind this cluster. The original Niari ZIP is now available; only the more specific representation/control relation remains unresolved.
